notes: Chosen hook '9 NATIONS SIGN AI SUPPLY PLEDGE'. Clarity 8: readable at a glance, though 'AI supply pledge' is slightly vague (supply of what?). Curiosity 6: it states a fact and does not open a question. Concrete number 9: 'nine' is the number, and slide 2 names all nine signers. Promise kept 9: slide 2 lists the nine, and 'pledge' matches the joint-declaration framing on slides 2 to 5 (slide 5 says no binding rules). Reader stake 3: no effect on ordinary readers is claimed, and none is stated in the article. That is acceptable because the hook is strong on the other criteria. Compared with the others: option 2 (shared job) is vaguer and has no number. Option 3 (US, KOREA, JAPAN +6) is concrete but cryptic and hides what was signed. Option 4 (NINE NATIONS, NO NEW EXPORT RULES) has more curiosity and a number, but it is a negative frame that only slide 5 covers, and it risks reading as the main story. Option 1 is the best balance. Label check: options 1 to 3 are labeled honestly. Option 4 is labeled 'myth-flip', but no myth or common belief is established on the slides, so 'claim' or 'negative framing' would be more accurate. This is a minor note. hook_pick_reason contains an honest 'No reader-impact hook:' sentence, and no option is reader-impact, so it is consistent. Optional fix: if there is room, 'AI CHIP SUPPLY' or 'AI SUPPLY CHAIN' instead of 'AI SUPPLY' would remove the vagueness. This is not required.
